tag: Episode 14 · The Hand of the Void
title: The Hand of the Void

beats.t: A black thread stretched taut beyond the bakery window. Whenever it pulled toward the clock tower, the numbers on Yeoni's front hoof lost another digit.
Who are you?! Actually, I don't care who you are! Please do something about this!
That's why I'm here. My lady, your hoof, this way.
I'm not putting Yeoni in the hands of a stranger.
Then try cutting it with your claws, Mr. Cat. Her hoof will come off before the thread does.
The man opened his bare palm. A coin-sized hole pierced its center. Inside, it was blacker than the night sky.
There's... a hole in your hand. An actual hole.
The wind blew backward. The black thread curved toward the hole, then vanished into it with the slurp of a noodle.
[ Time held: 71:41:09 — Frozen ]
It stopped. The numbers stopped!
Ugh... Today's a little salty.
The man clenched his hand. Between his fingers, the edge of the hole had widened by the width of a grain of rice.
Does that hole get bigger every time you use it?
Sharp eyes. Yes, it does. That's why I use it sparingly. Only for ladies like you.
The shadow atop the clock tower tilted its head. Its cloak fluttered once, and it vanished behind the hands.
(It saw us. It watched us cut the thread, and just left.)
The next morning, the first steam rose from the bakery chimney. Yeoni tied on an apron and stood before the dough.
Fold with your wrist, not your palm. Leave the dough some room to breathe.
Room to breathe! Yeongnyangi says that all the time, too. Breathe, breathe, breathe.
Yeoni's hooves suited the dough better than expected. Something soft folding something soft produced neat, even layers.
Good for a first try. Better than Luna.
Sis! You said that was a secret!
A long line stretched past the window. Outside, Moka tapped a pot with his ladle as he organized the queue.
Around lunchtime, Luna's sister touched her wrist to Yeoni's hoof. Tick. The pending numbers turned into real ones.
[ Time earned by my own hands: +00:12:00 ]
Twelve minutes. Twelve minutes I earned.
You're that happy over just twelve minutes?
Not just. I'm not spending these. I'm framing them. In a frame inside my heart.
For the first time, Luna's sister laughed aloud. Only the corners of her mouth stood clear in her fading face.
Luna, let's take a roll to that man from yesterday, too. The one who cut the thread.
Yesterday? What man?
The purple tent. The glove. The man with a hole in his hand.
Someone like that came here? Sis, did we have a visitor yesterday?
Well... I don't remember. We must have been busy.
The merchant at the skewer stall across the way shook their head, too. A purple tent? There isn't a tent like that in this market.
(It was yesterday. We all saw him.)
The bakery door opened. The man from the purple tent came in yawning. Luna greeted him like a customer she had never seen.
Welcome! Is this your first visit?
Yes, my first. Every day is my first.
Mister. Everyone forgot you. In just one night.
I know. That's how it works. After a day, my face fades. After three, my name.
How can you say that with a smile?
If I cried, you might give me free bread. That would be cheating.
I remember. Every single thing that happened yesterday.
Today you do.
That was all Yundal said before picking up a roll. He held out his wrist, but there was no tick. The register could not read it.
Sir, your wrist is... completely empty.
Yes. So I always buy on credit. This lady will pay for me.
Keep your hands off my twelve minutes. Those are for framing.
That expression deserves five stars.
You too, Yeongnyangi?! Star ratings are my specialty!
Just then, the shop window rattled. A blue airship descended directly above the bakery, casting a shadow over it.
A rope ladder dropped from the airship's belly. A white rabbit in a blue vest glided elegantly down it.
Hello there! Blue Rabbit Finance. I'm here for the customer whose payment comes due today.
It's still today. You said I had until evening.
You read the back of the contract, didn't you? Collateral: one tomorrow. Due: noon today. And it's one minute to noon, isn't it?
The clock tower bell rang. Once, twice. Before the twelfth chime had finished, the rabbit snapped its fingers.
Shining sand spilled from Luna's sister's chest. In midair, it gathered into a small hourglass that slipped neatly into the rabbit's paw.
Give it back! Give my sister's tomorrow back!
Don't worry! She'll be perfectly fine today. She just won't have a tomorrow.
Identify yourself. Whose hand are you?
Oh my, what a perceptive cat. I'm the weakest of the Chairman's hands!
If we were fingers, I'd be the little one. Still, I can run an island like this all by myself.
Who's the Chairman?!
I'm not allowed to tell you that. But I'll tell you something nice instead.
The rabbit hopped up to Yeoni. Its pink nose twitched, and its eyes curved into crescents.
Oh, goodness. Your chart has an empty hour slot, doesn't it? That's why your luck always arrives a beat late, isn't it?
[ Year □□ · Month 丙午 · Day 乙亥 · Hour □□ ]  4/8
Blue Rabbit Luck Loans! We'll fill in the blanks for you. Just a tiny bit of interest. And a few of your tomorrows as collateral.
(They can fill the blanks? Then I'd be one step closer to home...)
Yeoni. Don't hold out your hoof.
Fill that blank with something borrowed, and you'll pay interest for life. I'm living proof.
The rabbit's ears pricked up. It studied Yundal for a while, then burst into peals of laughter.
Oh! Now I recognize you. Our Hour of the Rabbit customer! You're still on this island?
Hour of the Rabbit? What does that mean?
That's the hour he was born. Around five in the morning. I ate it instead of collecting interest. Delicious!
Yundal's gloved right hand trembled. His mouth still held its smile, but his eyes did not.
How did it taste? My dawn.
Like dew? A little salty. Someone must have been crying that morning!
My lady. Mr. Cat. Just knock that hourglass out of its paw. I'll eat the rest.
You dare pick on the weakest? Even the weakest has a fat wallet!
The rabbit swept a paw, and gold coins poured out, stacking into a layered shield. Someone's day was engraved on each one.
Metal, I can handle. I'll cut through the tangled grain first.
Yeongnyangi's claws slashed diagonally across the coin shield. It cracked but did not fall. The coins clung to one another and held.
Yundal thrust his bare hand into the gap. The hole swallowed one coin, two, dozens. The shield sank like a sandcastle drained of water.
Urgh... Quite a lot added to my tab today.
Hand it over! Give her tomorrow back!
Yeoni hurled themself forward. Their pig's head struck the rabbit square in the belly. The hourglass flew into the air.
But the rabbit's long ear whipped around and snatched it. The rabbit caught hold of the ladder.
The weakest is always quick at running away! I'll put her tomorrow safely in the vault. The deepest compartment beneath the clock tower!
The airship rose into the clouds. A drifting flyer stuck to Yeoni's nose. Short on time?
It got away... right in front of us.
Outside, Moka flung down his ladle. That rabbit and this island get minus five stars! His voice carried through the glass.
When night fell, the island's ticking slowed a little. Yeoni and Yundal sat side by side on the bakery roof.
Does your hand hurt?
Only when the hole grows. The rest of the time, it's just a little drafty.
What that rabbit said earlier. Is it true? That it ate your birth hour?
It's true. I downloaded that app three years ago, too. Customer Support: the Universe.
You too? So you're my senior?
I am. I just haven't managed to graduate.
Yundal looked up. In the sky above the island, constellations like clock hands turned slowly.
This was the first island I landed on. I didn't have enough time, so I borrowed from that rabbit. A day, two days, a week.
I couldn't pay it back. The interest grew faster than the principal.
So it took the collateral. The hour I was born. Around five in the morning, when my mother held me for the first time.
Yundal took off his glove and held his palm to the moonlight. Stars showed through the hole.
The gap where my hour used to be moved here. Empty time. The Void. It draws everything in, but nothing remains.
Seven of the eight characters won't open the door. The door home.
So you've been here for three years...
At least my compatibility readings have improved. Three years of asking people for their birth dates and times.
Is that something to brag about?
The tip of a navy hat rose over the roof's edge. Yeongnyangi approached silently and sat between them.
Is that hole why people forget you, too?
Mr. Cat has joined us. Yes. Without an hour, there's no hook for a memory to catch on. I slip out of people's minds.
Yundal is an alias, too. It means leap month. A month that's there, yet isn't. Suits me perfectly.
Then what's your real name?
In the vault with my birth hour. The deepest compartment beneath the clock tower. That rabbit helpfully told us earlier.
I've heard a beast guards the vault. A beast with a ledger.
Yes. Black cloak, stripes. It records every bit of time collected in its ledger. I think you already know it, my lady.
(The shadow on the clock tower. The tiger.)
Yeoni looked down at the numbers on their hoof. Beside the frozen 71:41:09, a small twelve minutes glimmered.
I earned my twelve minutes. Her tomorrow is something she earned. And your name belongs to you.
The one who takes someone else's things is the thief. The one who takes them back isn't.
Then let's rob it. The vault.
Rob it? The clock tower vault?
Yeoni. Did you just say we should rob the vault?
Moka poked his head out of the window below the roof. I heard rob. I'm good at luring guards with delicious smells.
Ha... First plan like that I've heard in three years. I like how reckless it is.
It's not reckless. It's planless. I'll make the plan.
See? Yeongnyangi wants to do it, too.
Then the bakery's attic hatch burst open. Barefoot and in pajamas, Luna scrambled onto the roof.
My sister... She won't wake up. No matter how much I call her or shake her, she won't wake up.
[ Luna's sister · Today remaining: 05:59:59 ]
The number dropped by one. The today of someone whose tomorrow had been stolen was silently running out.
Six hours. We open the vault before dawn.
